title: Canonical ringed-site Cech comparison commutes with refinement after site pullback
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with final objects, finite fibre products and all objects, arrows, coefficients and index sets small in a common universe. Let $f:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be a morphism of sites given by a continuous functor $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ preserving the final object and finite fibre products. Let $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$ be sheaves of rings and $\rho:\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}\to f_*\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$ a ring-sheaf map. For module sheaves $M,N$ on these ringed sites [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $h:M\to f_*N$ be $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-linear via $\rho$. Assume enough injectives in both module categories [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Let $\mathcal U=(U_i\to1_{\mathcal C})_{i\in I}$ and $\mathcal V=(V_j\to1_{\mathcal D})_{j\in J}$ be finite coverings. Fix $r:J\to I$ and maps $a_j:V_j\to u(U_{r(j)})$. For a tuple $\mathbf j=(j_0,\ldots,j_p)$ write $V_{\mathbf j}$ for its fibre product and $a_{\mathbf j}:V_{\mathbf j}\to u(U_{r(j_0)}\times\cdots\times U_{r(j_p)})$ for the map given by the projections. Define the additive Cech cochain map [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex] by
$$\gamma(s)_{\mathbf j}=N(a_{\mathbf j})\bigl(h_{U_{r(j_0)}\times\cdots\times U_{r(j_p)}}(s_{r(j_0)\ldots r(j_p)})\bigr).$$
For either module category define $H^q$ as right-derived evaluation at the final object, using a nonnegative injective resolution, and define $e^q_{\mathcal U,M}:\check H^q(\mathcal U,M)\to H^q(\mathcal C,M)$ as $H^q(\alpha)^{-1}H^q(\beta)$: $\alpha$ is restriction of global resolution sections to the first-quadrant total Cech-resolution complex [def-sp-double-complex-total], with Cech degree $t$ first and differential $d_C+(-1)^t d_I$, and $\beta$ is its coefficient augmentation. Define $e^q_{\mathcal V,N}$ in the same way. The canonical map $h_H:H^q(\mathcal C,M)\to H^q(\mathcal D,N)$ is obtained by resolving $M,N$, resolving the termwise direct image of the resolution of $N$, lifting $h$ to that replacement, and inverting the resulting quasi-isomorphism on global sections. Then these canonical comparison maps are independent of resolutions and, for every $q\ge0$,
$$h_H\circ e^q_{\mathcal U,M}=e^q_{\mathcal V,N}\circ H^q(\gamma).$$
There is no acyclicity assumption on $M,N$ or the pulled-back cover. For abelian sheaves take the constant integer ring sheaves; in this case $h_H$ is inverse-image cohomology pullback followed by the map induced by the adjoint $f^{-1}M\to N$.

proof.text: The preserved product universal property gives the omitted-coordinate identities. Naturality of h and equality of alternating signs show the tuple formula defines a cochain map. Extensionality degreewise and at every tuple gives its uniqueness.

Apply the cohomological refinement component to this cochain map together with its tuple formula. Its nested unique-existence assertion gives the edges, roof and square. Uniqueness of the tuple-formula cochain map gives the outer unique-existence clause.

For abelian sheaves apply ringedSite_cech_refinement_square_abelian_exists to obtain the roof with its all-resolution normalization and adjoint-coefficient formula. For uniqueness choose canonical source and target injective resolutions and one replacement roof from the existence clause. Both candidate maps satisfy the same roof equation. Cancel the target derived-comparison isomorphism followed by the invertible replacement homology map. The ringed-site case is the cohomological component ringedSite_cech_refinement_square_rest applied in step 2.
